steps.prompt: Which hero would you rather read about?
steps.a: Sam is good at everything. Sam is never wrong. Sam always wins.
steps.b: Sam is the fastest runner in school, but Sam never listens to anyone, not even the coach shouting "Wait!"
steps.reveal: Perfect characters are boring because nothing can go wrong for them. Sam's flaw (never listening) is going to cause trouble, and that's exactly what makes you want to read on.

cards.title: Flaws make characters real
cards.body: A flaw is a weakness: impatient, jealous, forgetful, stubborn, a show-off. Real people have flaws, so characters with flaws feel real. Readers often like characters more when they struggle.

cards.title: Inner and outer conflict
cards.body: Outer conflict is a problem outside the character: a storm, a bully, a locked door. Inner conflict is a struggle inside: fear, guilt, wanting two things at once. The best stories have both.

cards.title: The flaw gets in the way
cards.text: Kai wants to win the science fair. But Kai is impatient, so he paints the volcano before the glue dries, and the whole thing slides off the table.
cards.note: The want (win), the flaw (impatient) and the trouble (the volcano collapses) work together. That's a plot.

cards.title: Find the flaw in action
cards.prompt: Tap the two words that show Nora is jealous.
cards.text: When Mira won the art prize, Nora clapped slowly, glared at the trophy, and muttered, "Lucky."

prompts: How did your character's flaw cause trouble in your scene?
